title: Improvement of the improvement process
labels: SIMULATION — a synthetic improvement arena; policies and fixes are real executable code, the failure distribution is invented
Both policies and the arena were written by the same author. The result describes this testbed.

steps.claim: The candidate changes the evolution system's own behaviour and is versioned as such
steps.observed: evolution v1 → candidate; changed evolution.json, policy.mjs

steps.claim: Old and new policies get equal budgets and the same unseen failure episodes
steps.observed: 30 episodes from held-out set arena-A; budget 420 units each; mean spent 411.3333 (incumbent) and 372.8 (candidate)

steps.claim: What is measured is independently validated improvement, not the policy's own claims
steps.observed: validated benefit 165 → 177.6167 per 100 reviews (difference 12.6167, 95% interval 0.4167 to 25.4333); sign test: 11 better, 2 worse, 17 same, p=0.02246

steps.claim: The cost of unsuccessful experiments is counted
steps.observed: budget spent on fixes that failed: 207.3333 → 120.0667 units per campaign (difference -87.2667, 95% interval -113.3333 to -62.1333)

steps.claim: The decision follows the frozen rule, whichever way it falls
steps.observed: accept: Accepted: validated_benefit improved by 12.6167 against the incumbent (95% interval 0.4167 to 25.4333) with every hard gate passed.

steps.claim: The sensitivity check and known regressions are reported, favourable or not
steps.observed: without the unverified complaint class: difference 5.6167 (95% interval -5.15 to 16.65). In 2 of 30 episodes the candidate policy delivered less validated benefit than the incumbent Without the unverified complaint class the advantage is not demonstrated (difference 5.6167, 95% interval -5.15 to 16.65)
